name: fixed
title: Compare a pattern as literal text

origin.description: fixed() treats the pattern as literal text. A plain character pattern is a regular expression; fixed() turns that off.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Text to match literally. A value that is not a plain character vector is coerced, with a warning.

arguments.name: ignore_case
arguments.text: If TRUE, ignore case with a one-to-one mapping between upper and lower case letters.

origin.details: The object is a character vector of classes stringr_fixed, stringr_pattern, and character. Its options attribute is the stringi fixed-pattern list, and that list always contains case_insensitive. TRUE becomes the pattern "TRUE", FALSE becomes "FALSE", and NULL becomes an empty character vector.
origin.value: The pattern, with case_insensitive taken from ignore_case.

translation.description: fixed() treats the pattern as literal text and stores case_insensitive for the stringi fixed searcher.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Text to match literally. A string or a list of strings is kept. True becomes "TRUE", False becomes "FALSE", and None becomes an empty list, with a warning.

arguments.name: ignore_case
arguments.text: If True, ignore case with a one-code-point mapping. The value must be True or False.

translation.details: The result is a Pattern whose kind is fixed. options is the dict from stri_opts_fixed, and case_insensitive is always present. A missing pattern is stringi's NA, not the letters NA.
translation.value: A Pattern. The text is the pattern, and options["case_insensitive"] follows ignore_case.
translation.example:
from stringr.pattern import fixed
fixed("a.b", ignore_case=True)
